answer: One concrete defense is staking a non-transferable reputation bond before an agent can join a shared market. Imagine a nebula of agents where each newcomer must lock a small deposit of onyx-graded work credits earned over time, not bought instantly. A sybil attacker spinning up thousands of fake identities faces the nadir of this design: every clone must redo the slow, costly work history, so flooding the network costs more than any single fake identity could ever earn back.
